missionPremise: Smart Files is a BUILD, not a rendering pass (OPS-17 amendment A-002, line 189), and a NEW atom family that does not extend brokerage_workspaces (A-012, line 199). Doc 34 approved claims are not revised; the build is made true (A-003, line 190). The premise was re-verified by this lane at source on the actual build base rather than inherited: brokerage_workspace_attachments on origin/main @ 4dfb118c (lib/db/src/schema/brokerageWorkspaces.ts:54-76) has 8 columns (id, workspace_id, kind, uri, body, title, created_by_install_id, created_at), a single notNull FK to ONE workspace on cascade delete, and no updated_at, no version, no cid, no access_policy. The premise HOLDS.
completionPredicate: G-14 is done when a Smart Files contract type and artifact store exist such that (1) one document row supports N placements with the artifact row count invariant under re-placement, (2) a revision supersedes without destroying and the prior version is retrievable by version identity, (3) every served artifact carries source + computedAt + servedAt with a STALE indicator proven able to fire AND proven silent on a fresh artifact, (4) accessPolicy is a column on the record resolved at read time, and (5) the entityId shape is written down before the first schema PR. A stranger evaluates this by running the probes in the frozen WDLL subset, not by reading a PR. AT CLOSE: 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are met and PROVEN in CI. The applied-to-deployment-database half of card item 2 is NOT met.

The pre-existing ten-item WDLL draft card covered five rows, so it was SUBSET rather than inherited or superseded (DEV_PROCESS 3.3b): inheriting it whole would have graded this lane on rows the dispatch declared out of scope, and authoring a second card would have produced two non-comparable cards for one lane. The boundary is the artifact-store contract: what the store must structurally guarantee is IN; what is put into it, counted from it, served from it, and sold on it are OUT.

wdllGrading.grade: PARTIALLY MET — merged and CI-verified, NOT applied to the deployment database
wdllGrading.evidence: smart_file_documents carries updated_at and access_policy; smart_file_versions carries version and content_cid. A CI probe reads information_schema.columns against the BUILT schema and asserts all four present. CI conclusion string SUCCESS.

But agreement is not execution.

wdllGrading.title: A document placed in N locations is stored once, not N times
wdllGrading.grade: MET AND PROVEN AGAINST A REAL DATABASE
wdllGrading.evidence: CI probe stores one document, places it in three locations, and asserts documents=1, placements=3, versions=1. A second probe places a FOURTH time and asserts the document count is still 1. Counting rules stated inline at each assertion (rows in the named table matching the declared entityId, measured — never derived by subtraction).
wdllGrading.structuralProof: Enforced by the DATABASE, not by caller discipline: a unique index on smart_file_documents.entity_id refused a second document row with PG SQLSTATE 23505, and a unique index on (document_id, target_type, target_id) refused a duplicate placement with 23505. Both refusals appear in the CI Postgres server log, so the negative cases fired for the right reason rather than passing vacuously. Without the placement uniqueness, 'placed in three locations' could legitimately have read as four.

wdllGrading.title: Revise once, current everywhere, prior version still retrievable
wdllGrading.grade: MET AND PROVEN AGAINST A REAL DATABASE
wdllGrading.evidence: CI probe places a document at three targets, revises once, then resolves all three placements through document.current_version and asserts every one reads content_cid `bafydoc-v2`. A second probe fetches version 1 by version identity and asserts the pre-revision content `bafydoc-v1` is intact with superseded_at non-null, and that both versions coexist (count=2). A third asserts re-inserting version 1 is refused with 23505 — history cannot be overwritten.
wdllGrading.structuralProof: Placements reference the DOCUMENT, never a version, so revise-once-current-everywhere falls out of the schema rather than needing a per-placement fan-out that could partially fail. reviseDocument performs supersede + insert + pointer move in ONE transaction with SELECT FOR UPDATE on the document row.
wdllGrading.note: Supersession is recorded as a POSITIVE fact (superseded_at) rather than inferred from the pointer.

wdllGrading.title: Every served artifact carries source, computedAt and servedAt, and the STALE indicator is PROVEN in BOTH directions
wdllGrading.grade: MET at the store read path, per the CP1 straddle ruling
wdllGrading.evidence: 23 contract tests pass (real exit code 0). The indicator fires on a stamp backdated 45 days past a 30-day threshold and stays silent on a 1-day-old stamp; the boundary is asserted exclusive (60s = not stale, 61s = stale). Unparseable stamps THROW rather than defaulting to fresh, and a non-positive threshold is rejected. readDocument builds the stamp unconditionally and SMART_FILE_READ_SCHEMA requires it, with a test asserting a stamp-less read is rejected. servedAt is taken as an argument, never read from a clock inside the evaluator — which is what makes the backdate test possible at all.
wdllGrading.mutationTested: The load-bearing verification. Replacing `isStale: ageSeconds > threshold` with `isStale: true` made the suite fail on REAL EXIT CODE 1 (not a pipe's), and the two failures were exactly the silence-direction cases. A fire-only test would have passed a permanently-firing indicator; this proves the gate can fail for the right reason (DEV_PROCESS 2.2, 2.3). Original expression restored and re-verified at line 273; final run green.
wdllGrading.straddleRuling: The source card probed 'the deployed serving path'. This dispatch builds and deploys nothing, so that reading was unsatisfiable in scope; the probe was re-pointed to the store read path and the residual obligation recorded, NOT dropped.
wdllGrading.residualObligation: G-53 must re-probe freshness on the DEPLOYED SERVING REVISION. This store-level pass does NOT satisfy DEV_PROCESS 4.4.

findings.title: A working CID content-addressing pipeline already existed; the brief presented brokerage_workspace_attachments as the only prior art
findings.evidence: dataroom_document_atoms (lib/db/src/schema/dataroomDocumentAtoms.ts) carries atom_did, access_policy, source_document_cid, storage_relation, widthed confidence and verification_status with a unique index on (document_id, atom_did) for idempotent upsert, fed by engine POST /v1/document-ingest. The mechanism is @hauska-engine/document-ingest: pinBlob mints `bafydoc-<sha256>` and dedups on content hash (gcs-blob-store.ts:65-66, in-memory-storage.ts:35); atom DIDs are sha256(`<sourceDocumentCid>:<atomContentHash>`).slice(0,32) (mint.ts:129).
findings.why_it_matters: Re-minting content addressing alongside a working deterministic-DID pipeline is the rebuild-instead-of-operate failure. OR-A2 ruled reuse; the store records an engine-minted CID and implements no content addressing of its own.
findings.importantCaveat: attached_documents was NOT extendable either — read at source it has the IDENTICAL defect (single notNull engagement FK on cascade, no updated_at, no version, no access_policy) and is engagement-scoped rather than city-scoped. The reusable asset was the MECHANISM, never the parent table. Reuse-the-mechanism / new-parent is exactly what shipped.

findings.title: ACCESS_POLICY_SCHEMA is re-literalled in three subtrees of the atom contract with no divergence test
findings.evidence: grep -rln 'ACCESS_POLICY_SCHEMA = z.enum' over hauska-atom-contract/src returns conformance/common.ts, encumbrances/common.ts, workspace/common.ts, against one canonical type at registration.ts:56. encumbrances additionally narrows to a two-value EncumbranceAccessPolicy (common.ts:82).
findings.why_it_matters: DEV_PROCESS 2.4: one rule with multiple implementations needs a divergence test, and there is none. A sixth value or a reordering propagates to some subtrees and not others, silently.
findings.handledInLane: Smart Files did NOT add a fourth copy. It imports the AccessPolicy type and guards its own value list with `as const satisfies ReadonlyArray<AccessPolicy>`, which is a COMPILE-TIME divergence test: if the contract's union changes, the build fails. That is a mechanism, not a reminder.

findings.title: The document-ingest mechanism is reachable only over HTTP, not as a package dependency
findings.evidence: @hauska-engine/document-ingest is `"private": true`; its blob index writes `document_blobs` in the ENGINE's database (pg-blob-index.ts:2-3). legacy-design-tools has ZERO dependency on any hauska-engine package. dataroomIngest.ts reaches it via postEngineSpine over process.env.ENGINE_API_URL.
findings.why_it_matters: OR-A2 is honored, but a later lane must not try to add a package dependency that does not exist. The CID is minted engine-side over the gate-front seam.
findings.bonus: port.ts separates DocumentBlobStore (pinBlob/fetchBlob, content-hash idempotent) from DocumentAtomStore (claim atoms), so Smart Files needs only the blob half and does not drag in the classification pipeline.

challengesAtClose.challenge: Green CI on a suite whose probes might have skipped would be a vacuous pass. Did the 11 probes actually RUN?
challengesAtClose.resolution: Checked directly rather than trusting the aggregate. The CI log shows `✓ smartFiles.integration.test.ts (11 tests) 9613ms` — 9.6 seconds of real database work, not a skip — and the CI Postgres server log independently records six constraint refusals (three 23505 unique violations, two check-constraint violations, one NOT NULL violation) against distinct test schema names. The negative cases fired for the right reason in the database itself. This was the single most important verification in the lane, because a skipped integration suite is indistinguishable from a passing one in a green checkmark.

challengesAtClose.challenge: Is the store-once guarantee real, or does it merely reflect disciplined application code?
challengesAtClose.resolution: Real and database-enforced. The probes execute raw SQL against the built tables rather than calling the store module, precisely so that a disciplined store cannot mask a permissive schema. The unique indexes refused the violations at the database layer.

challengesAtClose.challenge: Does anything in this close overclaim against A-003?
challengesAtClose.resolution: No, and it is stated in three places. The store makes the three doc-34 sentences STRUCTURALLY POSSIBLE; it does not make them true for a customer, which additionally requires a corpus (G-44) and a served surface (G-53). Nothing here is customer-visible, so nothing here satisfies DEV_PROCESS 4.4, and no Smart Files collateral is unblocked by this close.

challengesAtClose.challenge: The hand-edited fixture was the largest single risk. Was it validated or merely hoped?
challengesAtClose.resolution: Validated three ways and then confirmed by an independent gate. Structurally (ordering, FK targets, paren balance, no duplicate names), by reconciliation against the migration (column parity 9/11/7 and index-name parity 9=9), and finally by CI's own fixture-drift check, which dumped the live pushed database and reported `Schema fixture matches live DB.` That gate is stronger than my validation because it is byte-level against pg_dump output.

challengesAtClose.challenge: Could a caller mistake a missing document for an honest absence?
challengesAtClose.resolution: readDocument returns null, and the store header plus the PR body state explicitly that this is NOT a typed absence and must not be rendered as a data gap until G-34. That is a DOCUMENTED constraint, not an enforced one — weaker than a mechanism, and reported as such rather than claimed safe. This is the honest weak point of the delivery.
